papers.title_zh: 尼塞韦单抗 免疫后第一年和第二年的结果。
papers.source_body_en: IMPORTANCE: The consistency of nirsevimab effectiveness across consecutive seasons and its broader clinical protective effects remain to be fully characterized. OBJECTIVE: To assess whether first-season effectiveness of nirsevimab against respiratory syncytial virus (RSV)-lower respiratory tract infection (LRTI)-related hospitalizations is maintained during a new RSV season, whether the effectiveness persists beyond the first season, and whether nirsevimab exposure is associated with hospitalizations for non-RSV infections and asthma during the first and second years of follow-up. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This cohort study analyzed 2 nationwide matched cohorts using the French National Health Data System, including infants born in metropolitan France before the 2023 and 2024 immunization campaigns. Infants receiving nirsevimab were matched 1:1 to unimmunized infants. Both cohorts were followed up for 1 year after immunization, with an additional second year of follow-up for the 2023 cohort. Data analysis was performed from February 2023 to August 2025. EXPOSURES: Single dose of nirsevimab. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: RSV-LRTI-related, non-RSV infection, and asthma hospitalizations were assessed using weighted Cox proportional hazards models. RESULTS: This cohort study included 74 672 infants in 2023 and 175 526 in 2024. At baseline, the mean (SD) age of immunized infants was 4.5 (2.0) months in the 2023 cohort; 19 633 (52.6%) were male and 17 703 (47.4%) were female. The mean (SD) age of the 2024 cohort was 4.8 (2.2) months; 44 863 immunized infants (51.1%) were male and 42 900 (48.9%) were female. Among 37 366 infant pairs in 2023 and 87 763 pairs in 2024, RSV-LRTI-related hospitalizations during the first year of follow-up occurred in 299 (0.8%) immunized vs 899 (2.4%) unimmunized infants in 2023 and 456 (0.5%) vs 1711 (1.9%), respectively, in 2024. Nirsevimab was associated with a lower rate of RSV-LRTI-related hospitalization in both the 2023 and 2024 cohort during the first year of follow-up, with effectiveness estimates of 66% (95% CI, 61%-70%) and 72% (95% CI, 69%-75%), respectively. An association with higher rates of hospitalization for ear, nose, and throat (ENT) bacterial infections was observed (2023 cohort: weighted hazard ratio [wHR], 1.36; 95% CI, 1.00-1.84; 2024 cohort: wHR, 1.43; 95% CI, 1.15-1.78). No significant association was observed for other outcomes. During the second year of follow-up, no protective association was observed for RSV-LRTI-related hospitalization (wHR, 1.03; 95% CI, 0.73-1.43). An association with higher rates of hospitalization for ENT (wHR, 1.56; 95% CI, 1.10-2.22) and asthma (wHR, 1.24; 95% CI, 1.05-1.46) was observed. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: This study found that nirsevimab was associated with a substantial reduction in RSV-LRTI-related hospitalizations during the first year across both the 2023-2024 and 2024-2025 seasons. It was not associated with reduced hospitalizations due to non-RSV infections or asthma, nor during the second year of follow-up.

papers.title: Molecular Surveillance of Respiratory Viral Pathogens Detected by Multiplex PCR During the Post-COVID-19 Period: Distribution, Co-infections, and Seasonal Patterns.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: The COVID-19 pandemic profoundly altered the circulation dynamics of respiratory viruses worldwide. However, data describing post-COVID-19 viral epidemiology remain limited. This study aimed to characterize the distribution, demographic associations, co-infection patterns, and seasonality of respiratory pathogens detected by multiplex PCR in the post-COVID-19 period. METHODS: In this retrospective single-center study, 750 patients whose respiratory tract specimens were submitted to a tertiary care university hospital between February 2023 and March 2024 were included. Samples were analyzed using the BioFire FilmArray Respiratory Panel 2.1 Plus. Associations between categorical variables were evaluated using Pearson's chi-square or Fisher's exact test. RESULTS: At least one pathogen was detected in 56.3% (422/750) of patients. Of 535 detected pathogens, 98.5% were viral agents. Human rhinovirus/enterovirus (30.3%) was the most frequently identified virus overall and predominated in pediatric patients (43.4%), whereas SARS-CoV-2 was most common among adults (22.9%). Influenza viruses (17.4%) and respiratory syncytial virus demonstrated marked winter predominance, while human rhinovirus/enterovirus and SARS-CoV-2 circulated year-round. Overall positivity and co-infection rates were significantly higher in pediatric patients (p<0.001). Co-infections were detected in 22.3% of positive cases. Significant associations were observed between viral distribution and age group, gender, hospitalization status, and season (p<0.05). CONCLUSIONS: Respiratory viruses continue to dominate the etiology of acute respiratory tract infections in the post-COVID-19 era, with distinct age-related patterns and sustained circulation of SARS-CoV-2. Multiplex PCR-based molecular surveillance provides essential insights into evolving viral epidemiology and supports ongoing monitoring of respiratory virus dynamics.

source_records.title: Respiratory infections
source_records.abstract: Abstract Pneumonia is diagnosed based on clinical symptoms and radiological features. It can be caused by a variety of pathogens including bacterial, mycobacterial, viral, fungal, and other atypical organisms. Most bacterial community-acquired pneumonia is due to Streptococcus pneumoniae, which is normally treated with penicillin and can be risk stratified using the CURB-65 score. Atypical organisms require macrolides. Hospital-acquired pneumonia involves Gram-negative or resistant organisms and treatment depends on local sensitivities. Viral pneumonias can include influenza and COVID-19, with antivirals used only in specific cases. Immunocompromised patients may develop invasive fungal infections such as Pneumocystis jiroveci pneumonia or invasive aspergillosis requiring targeted antifungals.

papers.title_zh: COVID-19 后时期通过多重 PCR 检测到的呼吸道病毒病原体的分子 监测:分布、合并感染和季节性模式。
papers.source_body_en: BACKGROUND: The COVID-19 pandemic profoundly altered the circulation dynamics of respiratory viruses worldwide. However, data describing post-COVID-19 viral epidemiology remain limited. This study aimed to characterize the distribution, demographic associations, co-infection patterns, and seasonality of respiratory pathogens detected by multiplex PCR in the post-COVID-19 period. METHODS: In this retrospective single-center study, 750 patients whose respiratory tract specimens were submitted to a tertiary care university hospital between February 2023 and March 2024 were included. Samples were analyzed using the BioFire FilmArray Respiratory Panel 2.1 Plus. Associations between categorical variables were evaluated using Pearson's chi-square or Fisher's exact test. RESULTS: At least one pathogen was detected in 56.3% (422/750) of patients. Of 535 detected pathogens, 98.5% were viral agents. Human rhinovirus/enterovirus (30.3%) was the most frequently identified virus overall and predominated in pediatric patients (43.4%), whereas SARS-CoV-2 was most common among adults (22.9%). Influenza viruses (17.4%) and respiratory syncytial virus demonstrated marked winter predominance, while human rhinovirus/enterovirus and SARS-CoV-2 circulated year-round. Overall positivity and co-infection rates were significantly higher in pediatric patients (p<0.001). Co-infections were detected in 22.3% of positive cases. Significant associations were observed between viral distribution and age group, gender, hospitalization status, and season (p<0.05). CONCLUSIONS: Respiratory viruses continue to dominate the etiology of acute respiratory tract infections in the post-COVID-19 era, with distinct age-related patterns and sustained circulation of SARS-CoV-2. Multiplex PCR-based molecular surveillance provides essential insights into evolving viral epidemiology and supports ongoing monitoring of respiratory virus dynamics.
papers.abstract_zh: 背景:COVID-19 大流行深刻改变了全球呼吸道病毒的传播动态。然而,描述 COVID-19 后病毒 流行病学 的数据仍然有限。本研究旨在描述 COVID-19 后时期通过多重 PCR 检测到的呼吸道病原体的分布、人口统计学关联、合并感染模式和季节性。方法:在这项回顾性单中心研究中,纳入了 2023 年 2 月至 2024 年 3 月期间向三级甲等大学医院提交呼吸道标本的 750 名患者。使用 BioFire FilmArray Respiratory Panel 2.1 Plus 分析样品。使用皮尔逊卡方或费舍尔精确检验评估分类变量之间的关联。结果:56.3%(422/750)的患者中至少检测到一种病原体。在检测到的 535 种病原体中,98.5% 是病毒病原体。人类鼻病毒/肠道病毒 (30.3%) 是最常见的病毒,主要发生在儿童患者 (43.4%) 中,而 SARS-CoV-2 在成人中最常见 (22.9%)。流感病毒 (17.4%) 和 呼吸道合胞病毒 在冬季表现出明显的优势,而人类鼻病毒/肠道病毒和 SARS-CoV-2 则全年传播。儿童患者的总体阳性率和合并感染率显着较高(p<0.001)。22.3%的阳性病例中发现了双重感染。病毒分布与年龄组、性别、住院状况和季节之间观察到显着相关性(p<0.05)。结论:在后 COVID-19 时代,呼吸道病毒继续主导急性呼吸道感染的病因,具有明显的年龄相关模式和 SARS-CoV-2 的持续传播。基于多重 PCR 的分子 监测 提供了对不断演变的病毒 流行病学 的重要见解,并支持对呼吸道病毒动态的持续监测。

papers.title: Trans-resveratrol alleviates inflammation and improves skin barrier function via aryl hydrocarbon receptor pathway in human reconstructed epidermis.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: The aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AHR) is a regulator of epidermal homeostasis and a promising target for cosmetic and dermatological ingredients aimed at improving skin barrier function and reducing inflammation. This study investigated the potential of the natural polyphenol trans-resveratrol (RSV), a compound of cosmetic interest, to modulate downstream AHR signalling and restore epidermal integrity in a model of skin compromised by a pro-inflammatory environment. METHODS: A reconstructed human epidermis (RhE) was exposed to a cytokine cocktail (IL-4, IL-13, TNF-α) to induce a phenotype mimicking some aspects of atopic eczema, namely inflammation, oxidative stress and barrier disruption, features also prevalent in sensitive and reactive skin conditions. The effects of RSV were evaluated by assessing inflammatory mediators, oxidative stress-related markers, aryl hydrocarbon receptor signalling and epidermal barrier-associated proteins using molecular, biochemical and histological analyses. RESULTS: Cytokine exposure induced a pronounced inflammatory response, activation of aryl hydrocarbon receptor signalling, oxidative stress-related gene expression and dysregulation of barrier-related markers. Treatment with RSV attenuated the inflamed phenotype by reducing IL1A mRNA expression and IL-1α secretion, attenuating oxidative stress-associated AHR target gene responses through downregulation of CYP1A1 and CYP1B1, while maintaining AHR and HMOX1 expression and modulating barrier-associated gene expression, particularly by downregulating CASP14 and upregulating the tight junction protein occludin (OCLN). CONCLUSION: These findings provide mechanistic evidence in a human epidermis model that RSV can counteract inflammation, mitigate oxidative stress and support epidermal barrier homeostasis, actions mediated, at least in part, through modulation of AHR downstream signalling. This supports the potential of resveratrol as a multifunctional active ingredient in cosmetic and dermatological formulations designed to strengthen the skin barrier and calm sensitive or compromised skin.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addressed the need to identify cosmetic and dermatological agents that can restore epidermal integrity and reduce inflammation in compromised skin. It aimed to evaluate whether trans-resveratrol (RSV) modulates aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AHR) signalling to improve skin barrier function and mitigate inflammation.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study used a reconstructed human epidermis (RhE) model exposed to a cytokine cocktail (IL-4, IL-13, TNF-α) to mimic inflammatory and barrier-disrupted skin conditions. The effects of RSV were assessed using molecular, biochemical, and histological analyses.
analysis.methods: A reconstructed human epidermis was treated with RSV following cytokine-induced inflammation. Inflammatory mediators, oxidative stress markers, AHR signalling, and epidermal barrier-associated proteins were measured using molecular, biochemical, and histological methods.
analysis.main_results: Cytokine exposure induced inflammation, AHR signalling activation, oxidative stress-related gene expression, and dysregulation of barrier markers. RSV treatment reduced IL1A mRNA expression and IL-1α secretion, downregulated CYP1A1 and CYP1B1, maintained AHR and HMOX1 expression, and modulated barrier genes by downregulating CASP14 and upregulating occludin (OCLN).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted RSV’s effects as counteracting inflammation, mitigating oxidative stress, and supporting epidermal barrier homeostasis through modulation of AHR downstream signalling. They highlighted RSV’s potential as a multifunctional active ingredient for cosmetic and dermatological applications.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest RSV could be developed as an active ingredient in formulations designed to strengthen the skin barrier and reduce sensitivity in compromised skin conditions, offering a mechanistic basis for its use in dermatology and cosmetics.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was limited to an in vitro reconstructed human epidermis model, which may not fully replicate in vivo skin responses. The evidence strength is moderate due to the absence of clinical validation and reliance on a single experimental system.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated whether trans-resveratrol (RSV) can modulate aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AHR) signalling to improve skin barrier function and reduce inflammation in a reconstructed human epidermis (RhE) model compromised by a cytokine cocktail (IL-4, IL-13, TNF-α). RSV exposure attenuated inflammation by reducing IL1A mRNA and IL-1α secretion, downregulated oxidative stress-related AHR targets (CYP1A1, CYP1B1), maintained AHR and HMOX1 expression, and modulated barrier-associated genes (downregulating CASP14 and upregulating occludin). The authors concluded that RSV supports epidermal barrier homeostasis through AHR pathway modulation, supporting its potential as a cosmetic or dermatological active ingredient. However, the study was limited to an in vitro model, and clinical validation is needed to confirm these findings.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究解决了寻找能够恢复表皮完整性并减少受损皮肤炎症的化妆品和皮肤病制剂的需求。其目的是评估反式白藜芦醇(RSV)是否调节芳烃受体(AHR)信号传导以改善皮肤屏障功能并减轻炎症。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究使用暴露于细胞因子混合物(IL-4、IL-13、TNF-α)的重建人类表皮(RhE)模型来模拟炎症和屏障破坏的皮肤状况。使用分子、生化和组织学分析评估 RSV 的影响。
elements_zh.methods: 在细胞因子诱导的炎症后,用 RSV 处理重建的人类表皮。使用分子、生化和组织学方法测量炎症介质、氧化应激标记物、AHR 信号传导和表皮屏障相关蛋白。
elements_zh.main_results: 细胞因子暴露诱导炎症、AHR 信号激活、氧化应激相关基因表达和屏障标记物失调。RSV 治疗 降低 IL1A mRNA 表达和 IL-1α 分泌,下调 CYP1A1 和 CYP1B1,维持 AHR 和 HMOX1 表达,并通过下调 CASP14 和上调 occludin (OCLN) 来调节屏障基因。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将 RSV 的作用解释为对抗炎症、减轻氧化应激以及通过调节 AHR 下游信号传导支持表皮屏障稳态。他们强调了 RSV 作为化妆品和皮肤病学应用的多功能活性成分的潜力。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,RSV 可以开发为配方中的活性成分,旨在增强皮肤屏障并降低受损皮肤状况的敏感性,为其在皮肤病学和化妆品中的应用提供机制基础。

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: The study addressed the need to identify cosmetic and dermatological agents that can restore epidermal integrity and reduce inflammation in compromised skin. It aimed to evaluate whether trans-resveratrol (RSV) modulates aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AHR) signalling to improve skin barrier function and mitigate inflammation.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: The study used a reconstructed human epidermis (RhE) model exposed to a cytokine cocktail (IL-4, IL-13, TNF-α) to mimic inflammatory and barrier-disrupted skin conditions. The effects of RSV were assessed using molecular, biochemical, and histological analyses.
analysis_en.methods: A reconstructed human epidermis was treated with RSV following cytokine-induced inflammation. Inflammatory mediators, oxidative stress markers, AHR signalling, and epidermal barrier-associated proteins were measured using molecular, biochemical, and histological methods.
analysis_en.main_results: Cytokine exposure induced inflammation, AHR signalling activation, oxidative stress-related gene expression, and dysregulation of barrier markers. RSV treatment reduced IL1A mRNA expression and IL-1α secretion, downregulated CYP1A1 and CYP1B1, maintained AHR and HMOX1 expression, and modulated barrier genes by downregulating CASP14 and upregulating occludin (OCLN).
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted RSV’s effects as counteracting inflammation, mitigating oxidative stress, and supporting epidermal barrier homeostasis through modulation of AHR downstream signalling. They highlighted RSV’s potential as a multifunctional active ingredient for cosmetic and dermatological applications.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest RSV could be developed as an active ingredient in formulations designed to strengthen the skin barrier and reduce sensitivity in compromised skin conditions, offering a mechanistic basis for its use in dermatology and cosmetics.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was limited to an in vitro reconstructed human epidermis model, which may not fully replicate in vivo skin responses. The evidence strength is moderate due to the absence of clinical validation and reliance on a single experimental system.

papers.title_zh: 反式白藜芦醇通过人体重建表皮中的芳烃受体途径减轻炎症并改善皮肤屏障功能。
papers.source_body_en: OBJECTIVE: The aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AHR) is a regulator of epidermal homeostasis and a promising target for cosmetic and dermatological ingredients aimed at improving skin barrier function and reducing inflammation. This study investigated the potential of the natural polyphenol trans-resveratrol (RSV), a compound of cosmetic interest, to modulate downstream AHR signalling and restore epidermal integrity in a model of skin compromised by a pro-inflammatory environment. METHODS: A reconstructed human epidermis (RhE) was exposed to a cytokine cocktail (IL-4, IL-13, TNF-α) to induce a phenotype mimicking some aspects of atopic eczema, namely inflammation, oxidative stress and barrier disruption, features also prevalent in sensitive and reactive skin conditions. The effects of RSV were evaluated by assessing inflammatory mediators, oxidative stress-related markers, aryl hydrocarbon receptor signalling and epidermal barrier-associated proteins using molecular, biochemical and histological analyses. RESULTS: Cytokine exposure induced a pronounced inflammatory response, activation of aryl hydrocarbon receptor signalling, oxidative stress-related gene expression and dysregulation of barrier-related markers. Treatment with RSV attenuated the inflamed phenotype by reducing IL1A mRNA expression and IL-1α secretion, attenuating oxidative stress-associated AHR target gene responses through downregulation of CYP1A1 and CYP1B1, while maintaining AHR and HMOX1 expression and modulating barrier-associated gene expression, particularly by downregulating CASP14 and upregulating the tight junction protein occludin (OCLN). CONCLUSION: These findings provide mechanistic evidence in a human epidermis model that RSV can counteract inflammation, mitigate oxidative stress and support epidermal barrier homeostasis, actions mediated, at least in part, through modulation of AHR downstream signalling. This supports the potential of resveratrol as a multifunctional active ingredient in cosmetic and dermatological formulations designed to strengthen the skin barrier and calm sensitive or compromised skin.
papers.abstract_zh: 目的:芳烃受体(AHR)是表皮稳态的调节剂,也是化妆品和皮肤病成分的一个有前途的目标,旨在改善皮肤屏障功能和减少炎症。本研究调查了天然多酚反式白藜芦醇 (RSV)(一种化妆品化合物)在受促炎环境损害的皮肤模型中调节下游 AHR 信号并恢复表皮完整性的潜力。方法:将重建的人表皮 (RhE) 暴露于细胞因子混合物(IL-4、IL-13、TNF-α),以诱导模仿特应性湿疹某些方面的表型,即炎症、氧化应激和屏障破坏,这些特征在敏感和反应性皮肤状况中也很常见。通过使用分子、生化和组织学分析评估炎症介质、氧化应激相关标记物、芳烃受体信号传导和表皮屏障相关蛋白,评估 RSV 的影响。结果:细胞因子暴露诱导了明显的炎症反应、芳烃受体信号传导的激活、氧化应激相关基因的表达以及屏障相关标记物的失调。治疗 与 RSV 通过减少 IL1A mRNA 表达和 IL-1α 分泌来减轻炎症表型,通过下调 CYP1A1 和 CYP1B1 来减弱氧化应激相关的 AHR 靶基因反应,同时维持 AHR 和 HMOX1 表达并调节屏障相关基因表达,特别是通过下调 CASP14 和上调紧密连接蛋白 Occludin (OCLN)。结论:这些发现为人类表皮模型提供了机制证据,表明 RSV 可以对抗炎症、减轻氧化应激并支持表皮屏障稳态,这些作用至少部分是通过调节 AHR 下游信号传导介导的。这支持了白藜芦醇作为化妆品和皮肤病配方中的多功能活性成分的潜力,旨在增强皮肤屏障并镇静敏感或受损的皮肤。

papers.title: Clinical characteristics and risk factors for poor prognosis of RSV lower respiratory tract infection: a two-center study
papers.abstract: Abstract Objective Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of acute lower respiratory tract infection (LRTI) in children under five years of age. In this study, we investigated the value of simple and readily available clinical indicators in predicting poor prognosis in children with RSV-LRTI. Methods This was a retrospective cohort study of children with RSV-LRTI admitted to Children’s Hospital of Nanjing Medical University (April 2023–May 2024) and Gaoyou People’s Hospital (December 2024–June 2025). Demographic and clinical data were collected from patient records, and patients were stratified based on three adverse prognostic events: admission to Intensive Care Unit (ICU), prolonged hospital stay, and severe pneumonia. Results A total of 257 eligible children were enrolled, of whom 254 (98.8%) exhibited cough, 144 (56.0%) presented with wheezing and 194 (75.4%) developed febrile symptoms. 220 (85.6%) cases of RSV-LRTI occurred in winter and spring, with a higher proportion of cases occurring in infants under 1 year of age. A higher respiratory rate at admission was independently associated with ICU admission (Firth regression: OR 1.132, both P < 0.05), though this finding was limited by the small number of ICU cases. The presence of three concave sign was independently associated with prolonged hospital stay (OR 5.242, 95% CI 1.360-19.951, P = 0.017). Procalcitonin (PCT) was an independent risk factor for severe pneumonia (OR 1.616, 95% CI 1.074–2.837, P = 0.020). Conclusion Higher respiratory rate at admission was independently associated with ICU admission, and the presence of three concave sign was independently associated with prolonged hospital stay. PCT was an independent risk factor for severe pneumonia. These simple clinical indicators facilitate early identification of children at risk of adverse outcomes.

analysis.research_question_and_background: RSV is a leading cause of acute lower respiratory tract infection (LRTI) in children under five years of age, creating a need for simple clinical indicators to predict poor prognosis in RSV-LRTI.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This retrospective cohort study enrolled children with RSV-LRTI admitted to two hospitals in China between April 2023 and June 2025, collecting demographic and clinical data from patient records.
analysis.methods: Patients were stratified based on adverse prognostic events including ICU admission, prolonged hospital stay, and severe pneumonia, and associations were assessed using Firth regression models.
analysis.main_results: Among 257 children, 254 (98.8%) had cough, 144 (56.0%) wheezing, and 194 (75.4%) febrile symptoms; higher respiratory rate at admission was independently associated with ICU admission (OR 1.132, P < 0.05), the presence of three concave sign with prolonged hospital stay (OR 5.242, 95% CI 1.360–19.951, P = 0.017), and procalcitonin with severe pneumonia (OR 1.616, 95% CI 1.074–2.837, P = 0.020).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors conclude that simple clinical indicators such as respiratory rate, three concave sign, and procalcitonin can facilitate early identification of children at risk of adverse outcomes in RSV-LRTI.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings may inform early risk stratification and targeted interventions in pediatric RSV-LRTI to reduce severe outcomes and optimize resource use.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its retrospective design, small number of ICU cases, and single-season data, warranting cautious interpretation and prospective validation.

analysis.summary_en: This two-center retrospective cohort study in China investigated simple clinical indicators to predict poor prognosis among 257 children hospitalized with RSV lower respiratory tract infection between April 2023 and June 2025. The study stratified patients by ICU admission, prolonged hospital stay, and severe pneumonia, and analyzed associations using Firth regression. Among enrolled children, nearly all presented with cough, over half with wheezing, and three-quarters with fever. Higher respiratory rate at admission was independently associated with ICU admission, the presence of three concave sign with prolonged hospital stay, and elevated procalcitonin with severe pneumonia. The authors propose that these readily available indicators can support early risk identification in pediatric RSV-LRTI. However, the retrospective design, small ICU subgroup, and single-season data limit causal inference and generalizability.

papers.title_zh: RSV下呼吸道感染的临床特征及预后不良的危险因素:一项两中心研究
papers.source_body_en: Abstract Objective Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of acute lower respiratory tract infection (LRTI) in children under five years of age. In this study, we investigated the value of simple and readily available clinical indicators in predicting poor prognosis in children with RSV-LRTI. Methods This was a retrospective cohort study of children with RSV-LRTI admitted to Children’s Hospital of Nanjing Medical University (April 2023–May 2024) and Gaoyou People’s Hospital (December 2024–June 2025). Demographic and clinical data were collected from patient records, and patients were stratified based on three adverse prognostic events: admission to Intensive Care Unit (ICU), prolonged hospital stay, and severe pneumonia. Results A total of 257 eligible children were enrolled, of whom 254 (98.8%) exhibited cough, 144 (56.0%) presented with wheezing and 194 (75.4%) developed febrile symptoms. 220 (85.6%) cases of RSV-LRTI occurred in winter and spring, with a higher proportion of cases occurring in infants under 1 year of age. A higher respiratory rate at admission was independently associated with ICU admission (Firth regression: OR 1.132, both P < 0.05), though this finding was limited by the small number of ICU cases. The presence of three concave sign was independently associated with prolonged hospital stay (OR 5.242, 95% CI 1.360-19.951, P = 0.017). Procalcitonin (PCT) was an independent risk factor for severe pneumonia (OR 1.616, 95% CI 1.074–2.837, P = 0.020). Conclusion Higher respiratory rate at admission was independently associated with ICU admission, and the presence of three concave sign was independently associated with prolonged hospital stay. PCT was an independent risk factor for severe pneumonia. These simple clinical indicators facilitate early identification of children at risk of adverse outcomes.

papers.title: Recent Advances in CRISPR/Cas Systems for Respiratory Pathogen Diagnostics
papers.abstract: Early, rapid, and accurate detection is essential for clinical management and epidemiological control of acute respiratory infections caused by pathogens. Traditional testing methods such as microbial culture, serological testing, and PCR are restrictive in terms of operation and logistics and are therefore not easily used in point-of-care settings. The CRISPR/Cas system is an adaptive prokaryotic immune system composed of clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats and their associated proteins, which has been used as a nucleic acid diagnostic platform with programmable sequence-specific target recognition and signal-amplifying collateral cleavage activity. Existing reviews have mostly focused on the classification of Cas enzymes or amplification strategies; in this review, a pathogen-centric approach was taken, covering viral pathogens (SARS-CoV-2, influenza virus, RSV, HAdV and VZV), bacterial pathogens (Mycobacterium tuberculosis, Streptococcus pneumoniae, Mycoplasma pneumoniae and Staphylococcus aureus) and fungal pathogens (Aspergillus fumigatus and Pneumocystis jirovecii). Key technological advances, such as isothermal amplification coupling, single-vessel integrated reaction designs, amplification-free digital detection, and electrochemical biosensor integration, are evaluated for Cas9-, Cas12-, and Cas13-based systems, with their mechanistic bases outlined. The current challenges that hinder clinical translation, such as sample matrix interference, multiple signal cross-talk, crRNA off-target effects, and the lack of large-scale validation studies, are critically assessed. At the same time, future pathways for portable, integrated, and inexpensive diagnostic platforms are suggested.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines the application of CRISPR/Cas systems for early, rapid, and accurate detection of acute respiratory infections, focusing on viral pathogens including respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) as a target entity. The central question addresses the suitability of CRISPR/Cas-based diagnostics for point-of-care settings in managing RSV and related respiratory infections.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: This is a pathogen-centric review evaluating CRISPR/Cas systems for diagnostic applications. It assesses technological advances such as isothermal amplification coupling, single-vessel integrated reaction designs, amplification-free digital detection, and electrochemical biosensor integration across Cas9-, Cas12-, and Cas13-based systems. The review critically examines challenges including sample matrix interference, signal cross-talk, crRNA off-target effects, and the lack of large-scale validation studies.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The CRISPR/Cas system offers programmable sequence-specific target recognition and signal-amplifying collateral cleavage activity, making it a promising platform for nucleic acid diagnostics of respiratory pathogens. Key technological advances in Cas9-, Cas12-, and Cas13-based systems are highlighted as foundational for developing portable, integrated, and inexpensive diagnostic platforms.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review identifies critical challenges hindering clinical translation, including sample matrix interference, multiple signal cross-talk, crRNA off-target effects, and the lack of large-scale validation studies. These gaps underscore the need for further methodological refinement and empirical validation before widespread adoption.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Future research should prioritize addressing sample matrix interference, optimizing signal specificity, and conducting large-scale validation studies to enable clinical translation of CRISPR/Cas-based diagnostics. Development of portable, integrated, and inexpensive platforms is suggested to enhance point-of-care applicability for respiratory pathogen detection.

analysis.summary_en: This review evaluates CRISPR/Cas systems as nucleic acid diagnostic platforms for respiratory pathogens, with a focus on respiratory syncytial virus (RSV). It highlights the system's programmable target recognition and collateral cleavage activity as key advantages for early, rapid, and accurate detection in point-of-care settings. Technological advances such as isothermal amplification coupling, single-vessel integrated designs, and electrochemical biosensor integration are assessed across Cas9, Cas12, and Cas13 systems. However, challenges including sample matrix interference, signal cross-talk, crRNA off-target effects, and the absence of large-scale validation studies are identified as critical barriers to clinical translation. The review emphasizes the need for methodological improvements and empirical validation to enable the development of portable, integrated, and cost-effective diagnostic platforms for respiratory infections.

analysis_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 这是一项以病原体为中心的综述,评估 CRISPR/Cas 系统的诊断应用。它评估了等温扩增耦合、单容器集成反应设计、无扩增数字检测以及基于 Cas9、Cas12 和 Cas13 系统的电化学生物传感器集成等技术进步。该综述批判性地审视了样品基质干扰、信号串扰、crRNA 脱靶效应以及缺乏大规模验证研究等挑战。
analysis_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: CRISPR/Cas系统提供可编程的序列特异性靶标识别和信号放大的附带裂解活性,使其成为呼吸道病原体核酸诊断的有前景的平台。基于 Cas9、Cas12 和 Cas13 的系统的关键技术进步被强调为开发便携式、集成且廉价的诊断平台的基础。
analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该综述指出了阻碍临床转化的关键挑战,包括样本基质干扰、多信号串扰、crRNA 脱靶效应以及缺乏大规模验证研究。这些差距强调了在广泛采用之前需要进一步完善方法和进行实证验证。
analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 未来的研究应优先解决样本基质干扰、优化信号特异性并进行大规模验证研究,以实现基于 CRISPR/Cas 的诊断的临床转化。建议开发便携式、集成且廉价的平台,以增强呼吸道病原体检测的护理点适用性。

This publication is available at https://www.gov.uk/government/statistics/respiratory-syncytial-virus-rsv-maternal-vaccination-coverage-in-england/respiratory-syncytial-virus-rsv-maternal-vaccination-coverage-in-england-march-2026-report Published 6 August 2026 This report presents monthly vaccine uptake data for the maternal respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) immunisation programme in England, focusing on the period up to March 2026. This report includes vaccine uptake estimates for pregnant women who delivered in the nineteenth month of the maternal vaccination programme in March 2026. Main points The main messages of this report are: 62.2% (25,566 out of 41,128) of women that reported giving birth during the survey month received a RSV vaccine uptake varied by NHS commissioning region, with the highest uptake reported in the South West region (72.5%) and the lowest in the London region (51.3%) uptake varied across integrated care boards (ICBs) with the highest uptake reported in the Cornwall and the Isles of Scilly ICB (77.8%) and the lowest in Birmingham and Solihull (39.3%) uptake varied across local authorities, with the highest uptake reported in the West Berkshire (84.0%) and the lowest in Enfield (34.3%) uptake varied by ethnic group, with the highest uptake reported among the Asian or Asian British - Chinese ethnic group (76.3%) and the lowest among the Black - Caribbean ethnic group (33.6%) Help us improve this resource This vaccine uptake report has been designated as an Official Statistics release. As part of this process, we are seeking feedback from users to ensure the publication meets your needs. We would be grateful if you could take a few minutes to complete a short survey and share your views. Please complete the survey Your input will play an important role in shaping the development of this publication. Thank you for your time and support. Analysis of maternal RSV vaccine uptake Maternal uptake of the RSV vaccine is assessed monthly to monitor the reach and impact of the national immunisation programme. Given the programme’s design, uptake is defined as the proportion of pregnant women who delivered in the reporting month and had received the RSV vaccine during pregnancy. This metric serves as a proxy for vaccine coverage by infant birth month, reflecting the extent of passive immunity conferred to newborns. This monthly report presents RSV vaccine uptake for women who delivered in the nineteenth month of the RSV vaccination programme in March 2026. The monthly uptake trend among pregnant women who have delivered since the programme’s launch is presented in Figure 1. Overall, the monthly RSV maternal vaccine uptake for March 2026 was 62.2%. RSV uptake increased in the first few months of the programme and has remained steady since October 2025. Figure 1. RSV vaccine uptake (%) trend among pregnant women by month of delivery, measured in March 2026 Note 1: the vertical lines represent a change in the percentage of GP (general practitioner) practices used to calculate RSV vaccine uptake. Up to December 2024, vaccine uptake was estimated based on data from a single supplier covering fewer than 40.5% of GP practices. From January 2025 onwards, vaccine uptake was based on data from more than 97.5% of GP practices and is more representative of national vaccination uptake. This month’s report includes data from both major GP IT suppliers, significantly expanding the data available in earliest reports (September to December 2024). It includes data from 98.9% of GPs in England, up from 40.4% of participating GPs previously in the first 4 months (September to December 2024) of the vaccination programme. This has been made possible by improvements in data quality and permits a more representative analysis of uptake and trends across England. To further explore variation in uptake, Table 1 presents uptake by commissioning region, while Table 2 provides the breakdown by ethnicity. As shown in Table 1, there are notable regional differences in uptake, with variation of up to 21.2 percentage points between NHS commissioning regions. Table 1. RSV vaccine uptake (%) in pregnant women, measured in March 2026, by NHS commissioning region Change to table view Commissioning region RSV uptake (%) North East and Yorkshire 62.9 North West 61.1 Midlands 59.1 East of England 64.5 London 51.3 South East 70.2 South West 72.5 Commissioning region RSV uptake (%) North East and Yorkshire 62.9 North West 61.1 Midlands 59.1 East of England 64.5 London 51.3 South East 70.2 South West 72.5 Variation in uptake by ethnicity was also observed, with a gap of 42.7 percentage points observed in the uptake between ethnic groups (Table 2). Table 2. RSV vaccine uptake (%) in pregnant women, measured in March 2026, by ethnicity Change to table view Ethnic group [note 2] RSV uptake (%) Asian or Asian British - any other Asian background 62.9 Asian or Asian British - Bangladeshi 53.8 Asian or Asian British - Chinese 76.3 Asian or Asian British - Indian 69.5 Asian or Asian British - Pakistani 46.5 Black or Black British - African 47.5 Black or Black British - any other Black background 42.7 Black or Black British - Caribbean 33.6 Mixed - any other mixed background 56.4 Mixed - White and Asian 57.1 Mixed - White and Black African 48.1 Mixed - White and Black Caribbean 44.9 White - British 69.7 White - Irish 65.7 White - any other White background 48.8 Any other ethnicity code 62.0 Ethnicity - unknown 57.1 Other ethnic group - any other ethnic group 46.7 Ethnic group [note 2] RSV uptake (%) Asian or Asian British - any other Asian background 62.9 Asian or Asian British - Bangladeshi 53.8 Asian or Asian British - Chinese 76.3 Asian or Asian British - Indian 69.5 Asian or Asian British - Pakistani 46.5 Black or Black British - African 47.5 Black or Black British - any other Black background 42.7 Black or Black British - Caribbean 33.6 Mixed - any other mixed background 56.4 Mixed - White and Asian 57.1 Mixed - White and Black African 48.1 Mixed - White and Black Caribbean 44.9 White - British 69.7 White - Irish 65.7 White - any other White background 48.8 Any other ethnicity code 62.0 Ethnicity - unknown 57.1 Other ethnic group - any other ethnic group 46.7 Note 2: the ‘Ethnicity - unknown’ group combines all records where ethnicity was not provided. This includes people whose ethnicity was not recorded, not stated, or who refused to give their ethnicity. The ‘Any other ethnicity code’ category includes individuals whose ethnicity has been recorded using non-standard or legacy codes (that is, codes not aligned with the 2001 or 2011 Census classifications). The map in figure 2 shows RSV uptake by ICB. Uptake varied across ICBs by 38.5 percentage points with the highest uptake reported in Cornwall and the Isles of Scilly (77.8) and the lowest uptake reported in Birmingham and Solihull (39.3). Figure 2. RSV vaccine uptake (%) among pregnant women delivering in March 2026, by ICBs Across the local authorities, uptake differed by 49.7 percentage points with the highest uptake reported in West Berkshire (84.0%) and the lowest uptake reported in Enfield (34.3%). The variation across the local authority are presented in the map shown in figure 3. Figure 3. RSV vaccine uptake (%) among pregnant women delivering in March 2026, by local authority Further detail, including uptake figures broken down by local authority and ICB, can be found in the March 2026 supplementary data tables. Since the RSV maternal vaccination programme has now been running for nineteen months (up to the reporting month), an increasing number of pregnant women are receiving the vaccine during their eligible window. This growing awareness and notification from gestation week 20 onwards have contributed to a gradual increase in monthly vaccine uptake from 40.5% in September 2024 to the current figure reported for March 2026. As the programme continues and more women are informed earlier in their pregnancies, monthly vaccination uptake is expected to gradually increase. Data sources and methodology More information is available in our quality and methodology information (QMI) report. The maternal RSV vaccination report will be released monthly, presenting vaccination uptake data only for the specific reporting month, without cumulative figures from previous months. The reporting period for the current report is from 1 March 2026 to 31 March 2026. This report focuses on pregnant women who delivered in the survey month, regardless of gestational age at birth. GP-level RSV vaccine uptake data is automatically uploaded via participating GP IT suppliers to the ImmForm website each month. ImmForm data is validated and analysed by the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) to check data completeness, query any anomalous data and describe epidemiological trends. Since September 2024, the reporting data collected includes: denominator: number of women who delivered in the survey month, excluding miscarriages and stillbirths, regardless of gestational age numerator: number of women receiving RSV vaccination from week 28 of pregnancy up until delivery refusals: number of women in the denominator who refused RSV vaccination between week 28 of pregnancy and delivery To ensure accurate denominators are extracted from GP IT systems by the automated survey and precise uptake estimates are calculated, the methodology uses a monthly data extraction process with a three-month reporting lag to allow enough time for relevant information to be recorded. For example, data from September 2024 was extracted on 1 December, 2024. The data presented in this report for March 2026 is based on data received from both major GP IT suppliers, accounting for 98.9% of all national GP practices participating during the reporting month. The April 2026 maternal RSV vaccination uptake report is scheduled to be released on 3 September 2026. Background information The RSV vaccine has been offered to pregnant women in England since September 2024 to address the significant burden of RSV-related illness, hospitalisations and deaths, particularly among infants under six months of age and older adults, who are at increased risk of lower respiratory tract infection (LRTI) (see the Green Book on immunisation). In 2023, the Joint Committee on Vaccination and Immunisation (JCVI) issued a full statement recommending the implementation of a maternal RSV vaccination programme. This recommendation was based on robust evidence demonstrating the safety and effectiveness of RSV vaccines in protecting infants during their most vulnerable period. The vaccine is recommended as a year-round programme to be administered from 28 weeks of gestation onwards. This timing aligns with the optimal window for passive antibody transfer to the foetus, ensuring effective protection against severe RSV-related illness. From 1 September 2024 (the programme start date), all women who are at least 28 weeks pregnant are advised to receive the vaccine as soon as possible, with vaccination continuing to be recommended for all eligible women throughout pregnancy up until delivery. Additionally, the vaccine will be reoffered for every subsequent pregnancy to maintain consistent coverage and protection. This monthly report includes vaccine uptake data for women who delivered in March 2026. Programme delivery The programme is delivered through GP and maternity services, ensuring accessible vaccination opportunities for eligible pregnant women across England. In addition, the RSV vaccine is available through the community pharmacy delivery model at approximately 37 sites across two ICBs in the East of England. It is also available at up to 200 additional community pharmacy sites across the Midlands, North West, and London commissioning regions during the 2025 to 2026 expansion phase. Previous monthly reports are available at RSV maternal vaccination coverage in England. Since the RSV maternal vaccination programme has now been running for nineteen months (up to the reporting month), an increasing number of pregnant women are receiving the vaccine during their eligible window. This growing awareness and notification from gestation week 20 onwards have contributed to a gradual increase in monthly vaccine uptake from 40.5% in September 2024 to the current figure reported for March 2026. As the programme continues and more women are informed earlier in their pregnancies, monthly vaccination uptake is expected to gradually increase. Data sources and methodology More information is available in our quality and methodology information (QMI) report. The maternal RSV vaccination report will be released monthly, presenting vaccination uptake data only for the specific reporting month, without cumulative figures from previous months. The reporting period for the current report is from 1 March 2026 to 31 March 2026. This report focuses on pregnant women who delivered in the survey month, regardless of gestational age at birth. GP-level RSV vaccine uptake data is automatically uploaded via participating GP IT suppliers to the ImmForm website each month. ImmForm data is validated and analysed by the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) to check data completeness, query any anomalous data and describe epidemiological trends. Since September 2024, the reporting data collected includes: denominator: number of women who delivered in the survey month, excluding miscarriages and stillbirths, regardless of gestational age numerator: number of women receiving RSV vaccination from week 28 of pregnancy up until delivery refusals: number of women in the denominator who refused RSV vaccination between week 28 of pregnancy and delivery To ensure accurate denominators are extracted from GP IT systems by the automated survey and precise uptake estimates are calculated, the methodology uses a monthly data extraction process with a three-month reporting lag to allow enough time for relevant information to be recorded. For example, data from September 2024 was extracted on 1 December, 2024. The data presented in this report for March 2026 is based on data received from both major GP IT suppliers, accounting for 98.9% of all national GP practices participating during the reporting month. The April 2026 maternal RSV vaccination uptake report is scheduled to be released on 3 September 2026. Background information The RSV vaccine has been offered to pregnant women in England since September 2024 to address the significant burden of RSV-related illness, hospitalisations and deaths, particularly among infants under six months of age and older adults, who are at increased risk of lower respiratory tract infection (LRTI) (see the Green Book on immunisation). In 2023, the Joint Committee on Vaccination and Immunisation (JCVI) issued a full statement recommending the implementation of a maternal RSV vaccination programme. This recommendation was based on robust evidence demonstrating the safety and effectiveness of RSV vaccines in protecting infants during their most vulnerable period. The vaccine is recommended as a year-round programme to be administered from 28 weeks of gestation onwards. This timing aligns with the optimal window for passive antibody transfer to the foetus, ensuring effective protection against severe RSV-related illness. From 1 September 2024 (the programme start date), all women who are at least 28 weeks pregnant are advised to receive the vaccine as soon as possible, with vaccination continuing to be recommended for all eligible women throughout pregnancy up until delivery. Additionally, the vaccine will be reoffered for every subsequent pregnancy to maintain consistent coverage and protection. This monthly report includes vaccine uptake data for women who delivered in March 2026. Programme delivery The programme is delivered through GP and maternity services, ensuring accessible vaccination opportunities for eligible pregnant women across England. In addition, the RSV vaccine is available through the community pharmacy delivery model at approximately 37 sites across two ICBs in the East of England. It is also available at up to 200 additional community pharmacy sites across the Midlands, North West, and London commissioning regions during the 2025 to 2026 expansion phase. Previous monthly reports are available at RSV maternal vaccination coverage in England. Search Home Health and social care Public health Health protection Immunisation Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) older adults vaccination coverage in England UK Health Security Agency Official Statistics Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) older adults vaccination coverage in England: June 2026 report Updated 6 August 2026 Applies to England Contents Main points Help us improve this resource Analysis of RSV vaccine uptake by cohort Data sources and methodology Background information Further information and contact details Print this page © Crown copyright 2026 This publication is licensed under the terms of the Open Government Licence v3.0 except where otherwise stated. To view this licence, visit nationalarchives.gov.uk/doc/open-government-licence/version/3 or write to the Information Policy Team, The National Archives, Kew, London TW9 4DU, or email: psi@nationalarchives.gov.uk. Where we have identified any third party copyright information you will need to obtain permission from the copyright holders concerned. This publication is available at https://www.gov.uk/government/statistics/respiratory-syncytial-virus-rsv-older-adults-vaccination-coverage-in-england/respiratory-syncytial-virus-rsv-older-adults-vaccination-coverage-in-england-june-2026-report Published 6 August 2026 This report presents monthly vaccine uptake data for the older adult respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) immunisation programme in England, focusing on the period up to June 2026. This report includes vaccine uptake estimates for the routine cohort (individuals who turned 75 years of age since the programme start date of 1 September 2024) and the catch-up cohort (defined as individuals aged 75 to 79 years before 1 September 2024). Uptake data for both cohorts is reported as the cumulative figure measured up to 30 June 2026. Main points Between 1 September 2024 and 30 June 2026: in the eligible older adults (routine and catch-up cohort), the overall vaccine uptake reached 63.5%, decreasing by 0.1 percentage points from 63.6% reported in May 2026 vaccine uptake in the catch-up cohort reached 69.2%, increasing by 0.2 percentage points from the 69.0% reported in May 2026 vaccine uptake in the routine cohort reached 48.3%, decreasing 0.5 percentage points in this cohort (from 48.8% reported in May 2026) in all the eligible older adults’ cohorts, regional vaccine uptake was highest in the South West (68.3%) and lowest in London (49.4%) uptake in males was 65.4% and in females was 61.7% uptake in the most deprived decile was 50.3% and in the least deprived decile was 71.6% uptake varied by ethnic group, with the highest uptake reported among White - British (67.0%) and the lowest among Asian or Asian British - Pakistani (25.1%) uptake varied by integrated care board (ICB), with the highest vaccine uptake in the NHS Bath and North East Somerset, Swindon and Wiltshire ICB (70.5%) and lowest in the NHS North East London ICB (46%) Help us improve this resource This vaccine uptake report has been designated as an official statistics release. As part of this process, we are seeking feedback from users to ensure the publication meets your needs. We would be grateful if you could take a few minutes to complete a short survey and share your views. Please complete the survey Your input will play an important role in shaping the development of this publication. Thank you for your time and support. Analysis of RSV vaccine uptake by cohort RSV vaccine uptake in older adults is described in terms of cohorts. This is where a cohort is defined in reference to the age at the programme start date (September 1, 2024, as described in the Green Book on immunisation against infectious disease). The eligible older adults are defined into 2 cohorts comprising the catch-up cohorts (a birth group cohort of those who were aged 75 to 79 years before the programme start date) and the routine cohort (defined dynamically as those that first became eligible by turning 75 years on or after the programme start date). Owing to the dynamic nature of the routine cohort, the eligible individuals in this cohort will increase progressively through the year as more individuals become eligible. The current cumulative vaccine uptake, dates of birth and eligibility definitions for these cohorts are described in Table 1. Cumulative uptake in the catch-up cohorts of the RSV vaccination programme for older adults has been steadily increasing since the programme’s start. Uptake has risen from 22.6% in September 2024 to 63.5% by the end of June 2026. As the older adults remain eligible until they turn 80 years of age, it is expected that uptake in this cohort will increase progressively as they remain eligible for longer and have more opportunities to be vaccinated. Table 1. Cumulative RSV vaccine uptake for older adults in the routine and catch-up cohorts, measured at 30 June 2026 Cohort group Birth range of cohort Age turned in September 2024 Uptake (%) Routine cohort Adults turning 75 years old on or after 1 September 2024 75 48.3 Catch-up cohort 1 1 September 1948 to 31 August 1949 75 68.5 Catch-up cohort 2 1 September 1947 to 31 August 1948 76 69.1 Catch-up cohort 3 1 September 1946 to 31 August 1947 77 70.0 Catch-up cohort 4 1 September 1945 to 31 August 1946 78 69.8 Catch-up cohort 5 1 September 1944 to 31 August 1945 79 68.7 Total 63.5 The cumulative vaccine uptake among all eligible older adults (routine and catch-up cohorts) was 63.5% in the reporting month. This represented a 0.1 percentage point decrease compared with May 2026 (63.6%). The uptake within the stable, fixed birth-year catch-up cohort has shown a steady increase (increasing by 0.2 percentage points from the 69.2% reported in May 2026). This provides a clearer picture of progress unaffected by population changes and rolling eligibility. The combined uptake trend among all eligible older adults (catch-up and routine cohorts) is shown in Figure 1, while the trend in RSV cumulative uptake by cohort for the catch-up and routine cohorts is shown in Figure 2. Figure 1. Cumulative RSV vaccine uptake for older adults (both routine and catch-up cohorts combined), measured at 30 June 2026 As shown in Figure 2, uptake differed between the cohorts, reflecting variations in eligibility patterns. The routine cohort achieved a cumulative uptake of 48.3% which was lower than the uptake in the catch-up cohort (69.2%). These differences highlight the dynamic nature of the routine cohort, in which individuals become eligible over time, compared with the more static population of the catch-up cohort during the reporting period. Among the routine cohort, the vaccine uptake decreased by 0.5 percentage points from 48.8% in May 2026 to 48.3% in June 2026. In addition, the higher uptake among individuals who turned 75 years of age in September 2024 compared to those turning 75 years of age in the current reporting month reflects the natural lag between becoming eligible, receiving an invitation, and presenting for vaccination. This time-dependent pattern is expected and consistent with the rolling eligibility of people in this cohort and highlights the importance of allowing sufficient time for individuals to engage with the vaccination programme. These dynamics underscore why fluctuations in overall uptake should be interpreted with caution and why separate reporting for routine and catch-up cohorts provides a more accurate assessment of the programme performance. Figure 2. Cumulative RSV vaccine uptake comparing routine and catch-up cohorts, measured at 30 June 2026 To illustrate the rolling eligibility within the routine cohort, Figure 3 presents uptake by month of birth, showing uptake patterns as individuals reach the age of 75 years and become eligible. The oldest people in the routine cohort (those who reached the age of 75 years in September 2024) have had the most time to receive a notification and attend their vaccination appointments. As a result, their uptake is higher compared to those who only just reached the age of 75 years in the current reporting month. Figure 3. RSV vaccine uptake for adults in the routine cohorts (adult turning 75 years after 1 September 2024) by month of birth, measured at 30 June 2026 As shown in Table 2, uptake varied across the NHS commissioning regions, with the highest uptake reported in the South West (68.3%) while the lowest was reported in London (49.4%). Table 2. RSV vaccine uptake for older adults (routine and catch-up cohorts), measured at 30 June 2026, by commissioning region Change to table view Commissioning region RSV uptake (%) North East and Yorkshire 65.5 North West 59.7 Midlands 62.8 East of England 66.0 London 49.4 South East 67.9 South West 68.3 Commissioning region RSV uptake (%) North East and Yorkshire 65.5 North West 59.7 Midlands 62.8 East of England 66.0 London 49.4 South East 67.9 South West 68.3 Uptake varied by deprivation (index of multiple deprivation decile), with the highest uptake in the least deprived decile (71.6%) and the lowest in the most deprived decile (50.3%) (Table 3). This represents a difference of 21.3 percentage points between the least and most deprived decile groups. Table 3. This is the twenty-first in the series of older-adult RSV vaccination uptake reports that will be released monthly, providing cumulative vaccination uptake data since the start of the campaign. The reporting period in the current report is from 1 September 2024 to June 2026. Data is collected through the Immunisation Information System (IIS), which holds denominator data and captures vaccination events from GP (general practitioner) practices and participating community pharmacies across England, based on data provided by NHS England. Vaccine uptake is calculated by dividing the number of eligible older adults who have received the RSV vaccine by the total number of individuals eligible for the vaccination. The vaccine uptake is presented by cohort (routine versus catch-up) and for all older adults combined. Where relevant, figures also describe uptake within the routine cohort by month of birth to illustrate uptake as individuals become newly eligible when aged 75 years. The data was extracted on 28 July 2026 to include vaccinations administered up to midnight of the last day of the reporting month (30 June 2026). The 5 catch-up cohorts are defined by their birth year and age as of the programme start date. A more detailed breakdown of the different cohorts can be found in Table 1. This report presents the vaccine uptake in both the routine and catch-up cohorts. The routine cohort are defined as those turning 75 years of age since the programme’s start date. This cohort is currently comprised of those that are just turning 75 years of age, and those that are currently aged 76 years. As individuals in this cohorts are gradually becoming eligible as the vaccination programme progresses, some have not yet had sufficient time to be notified and present themselves for vaccination due to the rolling eligibility in this cohort. Analysis of RSV vaccine uptake by cohort RSV vaccine uptake in older adults is described in terms of cohorts. This is where a cohort is defined in reference to the age at the programme start date (September 1, 2024, as described in the Green Book on immunisation against infectious disease). The eligible older adults are defined into 2 cohorts comprising the catch-up cohorts (a birth group cohort of those who were aged 75 to 79 years before the programme start date) and the routine cohort (defined dynamically as those that first became eligible by turning 75 years on or after the programme start date). Owing to the dynamic nature of the routine cohort, the eligible individuals in this cohort will increase progressively through the year as more individuals become eligible. The current cumulative vaccine uptake, dates of birth and eligibility definitions for these cohorts are described in Table 1. Cumulative uptake in the catch-up cohorts of the RSV vaccination programme for older adults has been steadily increasing since the programme’s start. Uptake has risen from 22.6% in September 2024 to 63.5% by the end of June 2026. As the older adults remain eligible until they turn 80 years of age, it is expected that uptake in this cohort will increase progressively as they remain eligible for longer and have more opportunities to be vaccinated. The routine cohort achieved a cumulative uptake of 48.3% which was lower than the uptake in the catch-up cohort (69.2%). These differences highlight the dynamic nature of the routine cohort, in which individuals become eligible over time, compared with the more static population of the catch-up cohort during the reporting period. Among the routine cohort, the vaccine uptake decreased by 0.5 percentage points from 48.8% in May 2026 to 48.3% in June 2026. In addition, the higher uptake among individuals who turned 75 years of age in September 2024 compared to those turning 75 years of age in the current reporting month reflects the natural lag between becoming eligible, receiving an invitation, and presenting for vaccination. This time-dependent pattern is expected and consistent with the rolling eligibility of people in this cohort and highlights the importance of allowing sufficient time for individuals to engage with the vaccination programme. analysis.time: Published 6 August 2026; data period 1 September 2024 to 30 June 2026.
analysis.location_and_population: England; eligible older adults (routine cohort: individuals turning 75 on or after 1 September 2024; catch-up cohort: individuals aged 75–79 before 1 September 2024).
analysis.event: Official statistics report on respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) vaccination uptake among older adults in England, published by the UK Health Security Agency.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: Overall vaccine uptake among eligible older adults reached 63.5% by 30 June 2026; catch-up cohort uptake 69.2%, routine cohort 48.3%. Regional variation: highest in South West (68.3%), lowest in London (49.4%). Uptake by sex: males 65.4%, females 61.7%. By deprivation: most deprived decile 50.3%, least deprived 71.6%. By ethnicity: highest in White-British (67.0%), lowest in Asian or Asian British-Pakistani (25.1%). By ICB: highest in NHS Bath and North East Somerset, Swindon and Wiltshire (70.5%), lowest in NHS North East London (46%).
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: Report designated as official statistics; cumulative uptake data presented monthly; programme ongoing with dynamic eligibility for routine cohort; regional, demographic, and ethnic disparities noted; no explicit risk assessment provided in the evidence.

analysis.brief_en: The UK Health Security Agency reported on 6 August 2026 that 63.5% of eligible older adults in England had received an RSV vaccine by 30 June 2026 under the national immunisation programme launched on 1 September 2024. Coverage was higher in the catch-up cohort (69.2%) than in the routine cohort (48.3%), reflecting the programme’s staged rollout to those aged 75–79 before the start date and those turning 75 thereafter. Regional uptake ranged from 68.3% in the South West to 49.4% in London, with notable disparities by sex, deprivation, ethnicity, and integrated care board area. The report, designated as official statistics, tracks cumulative uptake monthly and highlights persistent inequities in access to vaccination among older populations.
analysis.summary_en: The UK Health Security Agency reported on 6 August 2026 that 63.5% of eligible older adults in England had received an RSV vaccine by 30 June 2026 under the national immunisation programme launched on 1 September 2024. Coverage was higher in the catch-up cohort (69.2%) than in the routine cohort (48.3%), reflecting the programme’s staged rollout to those aged 75–79 before the start date and those turning 75 thereafter. Regional uptake ranged from 68.3% in the South West to 49.4% in London, with notable disparities by sex, deprivation, ethnicity, and integrated care board area. The report, designated as official statistics, tracks cumulative uptake monthly and highlights persistent inequities in access to vaccination among older populations.

news.source_body_en: The UK Health Security Agency reported on 6 August 2026 that 63.5% of eligible older adults in England had received an RSV vaccine by 30 June 2026 under the national immunisation programme launched on 1 September 2024. Coverage was higher in the catch-up cohort (69.2%) than in the routine cohort (48.3%), reflecting the programme’s staged rollout to those aged 75–79 before the start date and those turning 75 thereafter. Regional uptake ranged from 68.3% in the South West to 49.4% in London, with notable disparities by sex, deprivation, ethnicity, and integrated care board area. The report, designated as official statistics, tracks cumulative uptake monthly and highlights persistent inequities in access to vaccination among older populations.

Nirsevimab-resistant respiratory syncytial virus B (RSV-B) variants have been identified in infants with breakthrough infections during routine clinical use, according to a nationwide observational study from France. The findings provide the first large-scale real-world evidence that resistance to the long-acting monoclonal antibody can emerge following prophylaxis, although researchers emphasise that resistant viruses remain confined to breakthrough cases. Nirsevimab, which targets a conserved region of the RSV prefusion F protein, has transformed prevention of severe RSV disease in infants since its introduction. Clinical trials and early implementation studies demonstrated high efficacy against RSV-associated hospitalisation, but concerns have persisted over whether widespread use could drive viral evolution. The multicentre POLYRES-2 study examined RSV infections in 1,023 infants aged one year or younger who tested positive for RSV during the 2024–2025 season in France, when RSV-B predominated nationally. Researchers successfully generated full-length viral genome sequences for 858 cases, including 419 breakthrough infections in infants who had received nirsevimab and 439 infections in infants who had not received the antibody. Viral sequencing was combined with laboratory neutralisation testing to determine whether identified mutations reduced susceptibility to nirsevimab. Resistance-associated substitutions were uncommon in RSV-A, occurring in just 1.0% of breakthrough infections. In contrast, resistant variants were identified in 12.5% of RSV-B breakthrough infections. More than half of resistant RSV-B viruses carried mutations affecting amino acid residue 208 of the viral F protein, while researchers also identified several previously unreported mutations capable of reducing susceptibility to nirsevimab. Importantly, no resistant RSV strains were detected in infants who had not received nirsevimab, suggesting these mutations emerged under selective pressure following prophylaxis rather than circulating widely in the community. One notable finding was the detection of an RSV-B variant carrying the F:N208S substitution almost one year after administration of nirsevimab. The authors suggest this demonstrates that resistant viruses can persist longer than previously anticipated, highlighting the importance of monitoring viral evolution beyond the immediate RSV season. Despite the emergence of resistance, the study does not suggest widespread treatment failure. Instead, resistance remained confined to a relatively small proportion of breakthrough infections, and the overall clinical effectiveness of nirsevimab remains high. The researchers conclude that integrating genomic sequencing with routine clinical surveillance will be essential as RSV immunisation programmes continue to expand. Monitoring resistant variants in real-world settings could help identify emerging escape mutations early, inform future monoclonal antibody development, and ensure preventive strategies remain effective against evolving RSV strains. While the findings warrant continued vigilance, the authors emphasise that the overall benefits of nirsevimab prophylaxis remain substantial, with resistance currently representing only a minority of breakthrough RSV-B infections. Reference Fourati S et al. Real-world emergence of nirsevimab resistance in breakthrough infections with respiratory syncytial virus-B: a multicentre observational study in France. analysis.location_and_population: France; infants aged one year or younger with laboratory-confirmed RSV infection.
analysis.event: First large-scale real-world evidence of nirsevimab-resistant RSV-B variants detected in breakthrough infections; study authors emphasize resistance remains confined to breakthrough cases.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: 1,023 infant RSV cases sequenced; 419 breakthrough infections in nirsevimab recipients and 439 in non-recipients; 12.5% of RSV-B breakthrough infections carried resistance (vs 1.0% in RSV-A); no resistant strains detected in untreated infants; overall clinical effectiveness of nirsevimab remains high despite resistance emergence.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: Multicentre POLYRES-2 observational study; genomic surveillance combined with neutralisation testing; authors recommend integrating genomic sequencing into routine surveillance to monitor emerging escape mutations and guide future monoclonal antibody development; resistant variants can persist beyond the immediate RSV season.

analysis.brief_en: A nationwide observational study in France has detected nirsevimab-resistant respiratory syncytial virus B (RSV-B) variants in infants with breakthrough infections during the 2024–2025 RSV season. Among 1,023 infants with confirmed RSV, 419 had received nirsevimab prophylaxis and 439 had not. Resistance was identified in 12.5% of RSV-B breakthrough cases, primarily involving substitutions at residue 208 of the viral F protein, while only 1.0% of RSV-A breakthrough infections showed resistance. Crucially, no resistant strains were found in untreated infants, indicating resistance emerged under selective pressure from prophylaxis. The authors stress that resistance remains confined to a minority of breakthrough infections and does not signal widespread treatment failure, but they call for expanded genomic surveillance to track viral evolution and inform future monoclonal antibody design.

news.content: Hong Kong parents should have their children vaccinated against respiratory infections as the city faces a triple threat from influenza, Covid-19 and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), a medical expert has said. Dr Mike Kwan Yat-wah, an honorary clinical associate professor in the University of Hong Kong’s department of paediatrics and adolescent medicine, warned on Saturday that the current summer flu season had yet to reach its peak. His remarks came four days after the city recorded its first child death from flu this year. “The number [of flu cases] remains high and there is no sign of it dropping yet, therefore it is unclear when the peak will arrive,” he said. Covid-19 and RSV cases were also at high levels, Kwan said, warning that Hong Kong was under threat from three types of infections. “We are now under the triple attack of flu, Covid-19 and RSV ... this triple whammy is happening in Hong Kong and neighbouring areas,” he said. He urged parents to have their children vaccinated if they had not already done so. View in App READ FULL ARTICLE Kwan said children could still be protected by receiving flu jabs for the 2025-26 season, before receiving vaccines for the 2026-27 season under the government’s vaccination scheme. “Parents need not hesitate ... Vaccines for [these two seasons] are different. There is also no need to space them apart for a specific period of time,” he said. Covid-19 vaccine supplies for young children have been temporarily suspended because the jabs have expired. But Kwan said other vulnerable groups, including elderly people, chronically ill patients and those who had caught the virus more than six months earlier, should still get inoculated. According to the latest data from the Centre for Health Protection, influenza activity in Hong Kong remained high after the summer flu season began on July 2. Of respiratory specimens handled by the public laboratory in the week ending August 1, 9.94 per cent tested positive for flu, slightly lower than the 10.65 per cent recorded the previous week. Twenty flu outbreaks were recorded in various institutions last week, mostly in care homes for the elderly. Covid-19 activity also remained elevated, according to the centre’s data. Infections began rising in June, with the public laboratory detecting 700 new cases in the week from July 26 to August 1. Hong Kong recorded 20 flu and 18 Covid-19 outbreaks last week as respiratory infections remained at high levels. Photo: Edmond So Eighteen Covid-19 outbreaks were reported in homes for elderly and disabled people over the same period. The laboratory has also recorded a rise in RSV infections since late June, when the number of detected cases exceeded 200, compared with a few dozen during the non-peak period. The number peaked at 323 in the second last week of July before falling slightly to 265 last week. On Tuesday, the city reported its first fatal paediatric flu case of the year, involving a seven-year-old boy who had contracted influenza A (H3). The boy, who had been in good health and vaccinated, first developed symptoms on July 27. “I hope this serious case does not undermine public confidence in vaccines. It is an isolated case,” Kwan said. Without commenting on the specific case, Kwan said some people’s immunity might weaken several months after vaccination. The city’s 2025-26 vaccination scheme began in September last year. He added that some people might be born with weaker immunity because of genetic predispositions. Kwan said experts might also need to analyse whether the currently circulating H3 strain had undergone genetic changes that could cause more severe reactions in patients. The Department of Health said on Wednesday that the government had procured 1.3 million doses of flu vaccines for the 2026-27 season. About 530,000 doses of inactivated vaccine from Sinovac will arrive in Hong Kong from later this month. Another batch of around 660,000 doses of inactivated vaccine from Sanofi will be delivered from mid-October. The remaining supplies include about 60,000 doses of nasal spray vaccine from AstraZeneca and another 60,000 doses of recombinant vaccine from Sanofi. The government has also announced that Covid-19 jabs offered to people aged 12 or above under its vaccination programme will be temporarily suspended after September 5, when the current batch expires. Supplies for children aged six months or above were suspended earlier. Covid-19 vaccination services under the government programme will resume in the fourth quarter of this year

news.content_title: U.S. FDA Accepts sBLA for ENFLONSIATM (clesrovimab-cfor) to Update its Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV) Lower Respiratory Tract Disease Indication to Include Children Under Two Years at Increased Risk for Severe RSV for Their Second Season
news.content: RAHWAY, N.J.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Aug 6, 2026-- Merck (NYSE: MRK), known as MSD outside of the United States and Canada, announced today that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has accepted a supplemental Biologics License Application (sBLA) for ENFLONSIATM (clesrovimab-cfor) to expand its indication to include prevention of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) lower respiratory tract disease (LRTD) in children under two years of age at increased risk for severe RSV disease through their second RSV season. The FDA has set a Prescription Drug User Fee Act (PDUFA), or target action, date of March 22, 2027. In July 2026, the European Medicines Agency (EMA) accepted the application to expand marketing authorization for ENFLONSIA in the European Union (EU) for the same population. ENFLONSIA was approved by the U.S. FDA in June 2025 and by the European Commission in April 2026 for the prevention of RSV LRTD in infants born during or entering their first RSV season. Regulatory filings are underway for approval in additional countries globally, as well as for indication expansion where already approved. In RSV season 1, participants were randomized 1:1 to receive either a 105 mg dose of ENFLONSIA (n=502) or monthly palivizumab (n=501) by intramuscular (IM) injection. As a leading cause of hospitalization among infants globally, there is persisting unmet need for RSV preventive options for both healthy and high-risk infants during their first RSV season as well as for children at increased risk for severe RSV disease through their second RSV season. RSV season is the time of year when RSV infections are most common, usually occurring autumn through spring of the next year in temperate climates. Timing and severity in a given community or region can vary year to year. About ENFLONSIATM (clesrovimab-cfor) in the U.S. ENFLONSIA is Merck’s FDA-approved extended half-life monoclonal antibody (mAb) indicated for passive immunization for the prevention of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) lower respiratory tract disease in newborns and infants who are born during or entering their first RSV season. For infants born outside of the RSV season, ENFLONSIA should be administered shortly before the RSV season begins.
